speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) when will the Ministry review the minimum annual leave entitlement of seven days provided for eligible workers under the Employment Act 1968; and (b) what factors will the Ministry consider in determining whether the minimum number of annual leave days should be increased.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Annual leave entitlements must be seen alongside other entitlements that similarly support employees in balancing their work and personal needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: These include paid public holidays, sick leave and parental leave, which we have just recently enhanced.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: First, could I just check whether the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) is concerned that by increasing the minimum annual leave entitlement, it will result in lower productivity in the company?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Because I think it might be the other way, that a more well-rested workforce will be a more productive workforce.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, I think three years ago, the Senior Minister of State shared in this House that the worry is that increasing annual leave entitlement would entail business costs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It has been three years, so I did give the Senior Minister of State a good break.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could he just share an update on what exactly are these business costs?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And also, whether – taking into account my first point – where a more well-rested workforce will be a more productive workforce and that might actually negate some of these business costs that MOM is concerned about?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, all this will work in concert to make sure that the person or the workers themselves are able to be more productive, while also ensuring that there is a flexible arrangement to allow them to have more balance of their work needs as well as personal needs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we are looking at it more from multiple angles, rather than just fixing the problem with more entitled annual leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I think that the concern is that while some have the luxury of flexible work arrangements – and I fought hard to legislate this right to work from home – I think the concern now is that, it is probably the lower-income workers who have this minimum of seven days of annual leave and who do not have, again, have the luxury of working from home.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, I hope MOM can look into this from that perspective as well.
